page: Amazon Web Services r6i.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The instance allocates 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, providing dedicated CPU resource assignments. Hardware flags include AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI for accelerated vector and cryptographic processing. The platform is provisioned with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, establishing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local instance storage or discrete GPUs, relying on external network volumes, and operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark testing demonstrates mid-range single-threaded throughput alongside multi-threaded limits stemming from the dual-core physical allocation. The instance scored 1595.0 in Geekbench single-core and 1888.99 in stress-ng single-core benchmarks, both aligning with the middle performance tier. Multi-core output is restrained, recording 3423.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 3847.15 in stress-ng multi-core tests. The DDR4 memory subsystem achieved 29.13 GB/sec in uncached read bandwidth and 24.53 GB/sec in large-block write operations, with cached reads peaking at 207.86 GB/sec. Data processing tasks demonstrated 27.99 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 4.0 million operations per second in Redis SET operations.

The hardware configuration offers high memory density relative to core count, making it a cost-efficient option when memory capacity dictates infrastructure sizing rather than aggregate compute parallelism. Because local storage is absent, persistent storage throughput is tied directly to network-attached volumes over the 2 Gbps baseline link. The instance is suited for memory-bound workloads such as in-memory data caching, mid-sized relational database engines, static web serving, and memory-intensive ETL pipelines.
